clue.text: Character to eviscerate Nazarene

indicators.note: to eviscerate is to remove the innards, so only the outside letters of Nazarene are kept

explanation.surface: A violent instruction to disembowel someone from Nazareth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tone can mean the general quality or flavour of something, its character.

clue.text: One needing floor that's hard and carpet free?

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose and allowed to settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fussy about flooring, wanting it hard and with no rugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet free' reads as no carpet, but 'free' is the anagram signal for AND CARPET; the question mark flags that whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dancing needs a hard uncovered surface so the metal plates on the shoes ring out.

clue.text: Message sensibly conveyed in this bottle

definitions.meaning: a ... fibre carries sensory signals through the body
bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.surface: A message in a bottle, conveyed sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensibly' is a pun: by way of the senses. BOTTLE is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves carry impulses from sense organs, and nerve also means daring or courage.

clue.text: Pull on weed relentlessly shackles donkey

parts.note: shackles are chains
moke is a British slang word for a donkey

explanation.surface: A chained-up donkey, with a sideline picture of someone puffing away at weed.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is old British slang for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who chain-smokes draws on cigarettes (weed, tobacco) one after another without a break.

clue.text: Covered earlier clothing left for Spanish gentleman

parts.note: hid means covered or concealed

indicators.note: the earlier word is clothing the letter, wrapping round it

parts.note: ago means earlier, in the past

explanation.surface: Someone earlier covered up with clothing they had left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the minor Spanish nobility, a gentleman by birth.

clue.text: Republican on camera coming round to sum up

indicators.note: the camera phrase comes round the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: something on camera is in shot

explanation.surface: A Republican politician, captured on camera, coming round to give a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: In short is a phrase meaning briefly or in summary.

clue.text: Genre briefly returned in horrific series

indicators.note: briefly says what the parse yields is the shortened name, standing for the full genre
returned in says a run sitting inside the words is read backwards

parts.note: the run sits across the end of horrific and the start of series

explanation.surface: A genre story, abridged and reissued as a horror series.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading horrIFIC Series backwards gives SCIFI, which 'briefly' says is the short form of the answer: a sneaky device where the wordplay gives an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a literary and film category, alongside crime, horror and romance.

clue.text: One trap set during harangue in spring

indicators.note: the pieces are set during the speech word, placed inside it

parts.note: to orate is to harangue, speak at length pompously
I is the Roman numeral one
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Someone laying a trap during a rant in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' is a verb, as in spring from, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to arise or come into being, as a stream springs from its source.

clue.text: Hunter and dog requiring no introduction

indicators.note: no introduction means the opening letter of the dog breed is dropped

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A famous hunter and his dog, so well known neither needs introducing.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a bird of prey that hunts small animals.

clue.text: Border teams helped to build new town

parts.note: a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

indicators.note: build says the letters of these words are put together in a new structure

explanation.surface: Border teams helping to construct a new settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Hemel Hempstead is a town in Hertfordshire, north of London, rebuilt after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemel Hempstead was designated one of Britain's post-war new towns in 1947.

clue.text: Left at sea, aim to make forecast

parts.note: on board ship the left-hand side is port
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned at sea, hoping to predict their fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left at sea' reads as abandoned, but it is the nautical word for the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foretell or give warning of something to come, a kind of prediction.

clue.text: Sons in poor health — would this bring on nausea?

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son(s), as in family trees
someone in poor health is ailing

explanation.surface: Sickly sons, and a question about what made them queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question: going out on a boat is what brings seasickness on.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by boat on rough water is a classic cause of seasickness.

clue.text: Singer in a wooded hollow heard

indicators.note: heard says the phrase is spoken, and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley, so this is A DELL

explanation.surface: A singer performing in a woodland glade.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is the British pop singer known for Hello and Someone Like You.

clue.text: Poor snail one Yankee cooked with onions

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a bad or mangled state, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sorry snail and an American, both ending up in the pan with onions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' scrambles SNAIL, ONE and Y. 'Cooked' looks like a second anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyonnaise is a cookery term for dishes prepared in the Lyon style, with sliced fried onions.

clue.text: Ruthless to spread lies about terrible truth

indicators.note: the coat word lies around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to coat is to spread a layer over something

indicators.note: terrible says the letters of truth are in a dreadful mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynic spreading falsehoods about an awful truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To spread' is a verb meaning to coat; 'terrible' scrambles TRUTH to UTTHR.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutthroat describes merciless, no-holds-barred behaviour, as in cutthroat competition.

clue.text: Make hit plays and perform amusing opera

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters frolic about into a new order

parts.note: to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Advice to a theatre company: produce a hit and put on a funny opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, set in a fanciful Japan.

clue.text: Weapon, returned to court, that causes bleed

indicators.note: returned says the weapon word is turned back to front

parts.note: an axe is a weapon

explanation.surface: A weapon brought back into the courtroom, the one that drew blood.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact money is to extort it, and to bleed someone is to drain them of money.

clue.text: Repetitive notes written about adult in private meeting

indicators.note: the notes are written about the letter, enclosing it
repetitive says the notes are repeated, written out twice

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale, so two notes give TE TE
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Monotonous notes taken about a grown-up in a confidential meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tete-a-tete, French for head to head, is an intimate conversation between two people.

clue.text: Discharge of gas put through drink

indicators.note: the gas is put through the drink, so it sits inside it

parts.note: rum is a drink
HE is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: Gas being bubbled through a drink, like a fizzy cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Fitting fresh cover for metal bearings

indicators.note: the cheeky word acts as a cover for the rest, wrapping round it

parts.note: fresh in the sense of cheeky means pert
tin is a metal
E and N are compass bearings, east and north

explanation.surface: Talk of a new protective cover for metal ball bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' here means cheeky, not new. 'Bearings' are compass points, not machine parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent means relevant or apposite, which is to say appropriate to the matter.

clue.text: Enquiry ended early on ring with no charges

indicators.note: ended early means the inquiry word stops one letter short

parts.note: a probe is an enquiry or investigation
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An investigation cut short, its targets let off without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No charges' reads as legal accusations; here it means fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro bono work, from Latin for the public good, is done free of fees.

clue.text: Servant goes with crowd for violent disorder

parts.note: to crowd is to cram or ram
a page is a young servant

explanation.surface: A servant joining a mob to riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of wild, destructive behaviour by a person or crowd.

clue.text: Right arm is not broken in heavy fall

indicators.note: broken says the letters of these words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An injury report: a right arm, apparently not broken after a heavy fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is a heavy downpour, a big fall of rain.

clue.text: What's taken into staff about to give treatment

indicators.note: the exclamation is taken into the staff word, placed inside it
about says the staff word is turned round

parts.note: a bar is a rod or staff
eh is an exclamation asking what something is, the same as What?

explanation.surface: A puzzle over what new staff are given by way of medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's' supplies EH, the questioning exclamation; 'about' turns BAR into RAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab, short for rehabilitation, is a course of therapy for addiction or injury.

clue.text: Inventive sort decorates Lancastrian houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone from Lancashire doing up their homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was a famous inventor, pioneer of alternating current systems.

clue.text: Reportedly steps over fence in dash

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is as it is said, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence

explanation.surface: Someone said to leap a fence at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: A STILE is a step built into a fence or wall to let walkers cross, common on British footpaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash can mean flair or panache, which is what style also means.

clue.text: Energy cuts must stop

indicators.note: the energy letter cuts into the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: must means have to
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A warning that power cuts have to end.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAVE TO is a sailing term: bring a ship to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave to is to bring a sailing vessel to a standstill, head to wind.

clue.text: Annoyed when struggling to find pain reliever

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: An irritated patient hunting for a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a medicine that soothes or deadens discomfort, an analgesic.

clue.text: Ice for this lolly?

parts.note: ice is slang for kill and lolly is British slang for cash, so this is cash paid for a killing

explanation.surface: An ice lolly, apparently, and what it is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a frozen treat; in fact 'ice' means murder and 'lolly' means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood money is payment made to a hired killer, or compensation for a killing.

clue.text: Goddess wants case dropped in Boeotian city

indicators.note: the case is the outer pair of letters, and dropping it leaves the inside

parts.note: Thebes was the chief city of Boeotia in ancient Greece

explanation.surface: A goddess wanting legal proceedings dropped in an ancient Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as a lawsuit; here it is the outer letters of the city name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth and cupbearer to the gods.
